verdict.rationale: PagerDuty documents a public REST API for reading and changing account configuration: users, notification rules, incident workflows, on-call lookups and manual incident creation. It also offers an Events API v2 that can trigger, acknowledge and resolve alerts, a versioning header, published OpenAPI schemas, and an interactive try-it API reference. The probe's 404s were on support-site paths; the OpenAPI spec lives in the api-schema repo, so they do not contradict this. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of driving the REST API end to end (the only community integrator report covers the Events API and complains that v1 and v2 keys can't be told apart).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The REST API provides a way for third parties to connect to a PagerDuty account and access or manipulate configuration data on that account.
add and configure users on a PagerDuty account, including how they're notified by PagerDuty - set up workflows for responding to incidents - find out who is on call and when they're being notified
manually create an incident without an associated monitoring tool
Follow up events can be sent to acknowledge or resolve an existing alert.
Browse every PagerDuty public API — endpoints, schemas, and code samples — and try requests directly from the docs.
This repository contains our OpenAPI defined public APIs.
